questions.prompt: Which keyword is used to declare an enum in C#?
questions.explanation: The 'enum' keyword declares an enumeration type, which is a distinct value type.

questions.prompt: What is the default underlying type of an enum in C#?
questions.explanation: By default, the underlying type of an enum is int. You can specify other integral types explicitly.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank to declare an enum named Status.
How do you cast an enum value to its underlying integer?
questions.explanation: You can explicitly cast an enum to its underlying integral type using standard C# casting syntax.

questions.prompt: Which underlying type can be specified for an enum?
questions.explanation: Enum underlying types must be integral types: byte, sbyte, short, ushort, int, uint, long, or ulong.

questions.prompt: Arrange the correct enum declaration with explicit values.
Declare an enum Color with Red=1, Green=2, Blue=3. Print the value of Green.

options: Converts an integer to an enum
Converts a string to an enum value
questions.explanation: Enum.Parse() converts a string representation of an enum name or numeric value to its corresponding enum value.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank to get all values from an enum.
Which attribute is commonly used to provide a user-friendly description for an enum value?
questions.explanation: The [Display] attribute (from System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations) is commonly used to provide a friendly name or description for enum values.
